Reddit vote fuzzing was an interesting and innovative idea when it first came out. On the surface, it seemed (at least in principle) to help fight vote brigading, spamming, downvote censorship, etc. Many people believe that it was eventually abused to increase censorship and cause a host of other problems.

So the question is this: what have we learned, and how can we improve upon it? What kind of tools would you like to see for moderators of certain "serious discourse" subs to be able to keep their conversations civil and valuable? What fancy (or unfancy) tricks would you like to see voat.co use to make this place better than ever?
How would you improve voat value and voat integrity?

Vote limitation is a pretty neat trick actually. It makes you think twice about what you choose to upvote and downvote. I hope this limitation will never totally disappear (or become negligible as the user base and the average user scores grow).

You can't really be a powermod here. You can only moderate 10 subverses at one.

Some simple steps I think might help:

1) Voat limits per subverse. I know a lot of this is already in place, but I think it needs a little more. Limited downvoats per subverse for everyone, regardless of CCP. Limited Upvoats per subverse but at a larger rate. Also downvoat limits should be based off CCP over time, rather than grand total. So if you want a large amount of downvoats to use, you would need to maintain a fairly active positive presence in that subverse.

The drawback of that idea is this.... it will give more power to more active users, essentially creating psudo power-users. So I don't know if that is a great idea. I do however like limiting the powers a little. It forces people to actually think about who and why they are down or up voating, and that is good for everyone.

2) More degrees of moderation. There should be many more options to a moderator than just deleting a post or thread. They should be able to lock threads with Mod comments. They should be able to lock a chain of comments, with mod comment. They should be able to tag users with Moderator wide flair that follows, so a user can be tagged like "Strike 1 - spam - Bob/AskVoat" and other mods see that. The user would also be able to see any tags (and who placed them) in their user page.

This would allow for what I like to think of as "gentler moderation". The option shouldn't be nothing or nuke it from orbit. Give mods more ability to correct actions rather than obliterate users and subverses will grow stronger.

3) Advanced Subverse Blocking. We need the ability to create basic "black holes" where a user can black list a subverse and then all comments, all links to, and all existence of that subverse be removed from their feed. If saw a black listed subverse is mentioned on a positive subverse, the comment could be collapsed by default and noted to the user as "Contains black listed material" or such. This would all be controlled by the users but some of the more horrible subverses could start auto-blacklisted by default (to allow them to exist without submitting the general public to their hate). I do not volunteer to be the one to make that call.

Generally #3 goes along with #2, except on the site-wide Admin level. The admins too should have more options than forcing everyone to see garbage or banning garbage completely.

Just my thoughts.
